cna.title: [EVEROS-2026-01] EverOS: unauthenticated websites can exfiltrate arbitrary local files via file:// ingestion and permissive CORS

descriptions.value: EverOS 1.7.1 (EverMind-AI/EverOS) is a local-first agent-memory service whose FastAPI HTTP API has no authentication by documented design. Two insecure defaults combine into browser-mediated local file disclosure. (A) POST /api/v2/memory/add accepts a content item with uri file:///...; with the default file_uri_allow_dirs=[] the empty allowlist is treated as allow-any-readable-file, so the file is read by the EverOS process, parsed, and stored as parsed_content, which POST /api/v2/memory/search returns verbatim (50 MB cap per item). (B) CORS defaults are allow_origins=["*"] with allow_credentials=True; Starlette reflects the request Origin and returns Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Any website a victim visits can therefore issue cross-origin requests to the loopback API, ingest arbitrary local files, and read them back — no credentials, cookies, or prompt required. Demonstrated end-to-end in headless Chromium from a distinct cross-origin hostname; attacker-chosen memories can also be written (context poisoning). Re-verified unfixed at upstream main HEAD 6ac3898 (2026-11-24).
